### 9 The Periodic Table: chemical periodicity — Multiple Choice: Easy

::: {.mc-question #periodicity-choice-easy-q1 data-answer="B"}
### Question 1 · Atomic radius · 2.1 Choice Easy Q1

Which statement correctly compares sodium and sulfur?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>Sodium has the smaller atomic radius and the smaller ionic radius.</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>Sodium has the larger atomic radius but sulfur has the larger ionic radius.</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>Sulfur has the larger atomic radius but sodium has the larger ionic radius.</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>Sulfur has both the larger atomic radius and the larger ionic radius.</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>B.</strong> Atomic radius decreases across Period 3. The common ions are <span>Na<sup>+</sup></span> and <span>S<sup>2−</sup></span>; sulfur's ion has an extra electron shell compared with sodium's ion.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #periodicity-choice-easy-q2 data-answer="C"}
### Question 2 · Basic oxide · 2.1 Choice Easy Q2

Magnesium oxide is added to water. Which statement describes the resulting solution?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>It is acidic because magnesium oxide is covalent.</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>It is neutral because magnesium oxide does not react with water.</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>It is alkaline because magnesium oxide forms magnesium hydroxide.</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>It is alkaline because magnesium oxide forms sulfuric acid.</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>C.</strong> Magnesium oxide is a basic oxide: <span>MgO + H<sub>2</sub>O → Mg(OH)<sub>2</sub></span>, so the solution contains hydroxide ions.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #periodicity-choice-easy-q3 data-answer="D"}
### Question 3 · Hydrolysis of phosphorus pentachloride · 2.1 Choice Easy Q3

Which observations are made when a sample of phosphorus chloride, <span>\(\ce{PCl5}\)</span>, is added to a beaker of water?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>No visible changes are observed.</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>Steamy fumes are the only observation.</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>A white precipitate is the only observation.</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>Steamy fumes and a white precipitate are both observed.</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>D.</strong> <span>\(\ce{PCl5 + 4H2O -> H3PO4 + 5HCl}\)</span>. Both products contribute to the acidic observation.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #periodicity-choice-easy-q4 data-answer="C"}
### Question 4 · Outer-shell electrons · 2.1 Choice Easy Q4

Which substance contains an atom whose outer shell is incomplete in a simple covalent molecule?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>\(\ce{H3O+}\)</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>\(\ce{CH4}\)</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>\(\ce{BF3}\)</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>\(\ce{MgO}\)</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>C.</strong> Boron in <span>BF<sub>3</sub></span> forms three covalent bonds and has only six electrons around it.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #periodicity-choice-easy-q5 data-answer="A"}
### Question 5 · Period 3 physical properties · 2.1 Choice Easy Q5

The three graphs show trends across Period 3. Which important physical property is not represented?

![Three original Period 3 trend graphs](../assets/questions/original-source/2-1-choice-easy-q5-figure.png){.question-figure fig-alt="Three trend graphs for sodium to sulfur"}

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>Electrical conductivity</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>Atomic radius</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>Melting point</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>First ionisation energy</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>A.</strong> The graphs show melting point, first ionisation energy and atomic radius. Conductivity is not shown.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #periodicity-choice-easy-q6 data-answer="C"}
### Question 6 · Formula and mole ratio · 2.1 Choice Easy Q6

Silicon reacts with chlorine to produce silicon chloride. How many moles of chlorine are needed to react with 1 mole of silicon?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>2</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>3</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>4</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>5</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>C.</strong> The formula of the chloride is <span>SiCl<sub>4</sub></span>, so one mole of silicon is combined with four moles of chlorine atoms.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #periodicity-choice-easy-q7 data-answer="A"}
### Question 7 · Oxide stoichiometry · 2.1 Choice Easy Q7

During the manufacture of steel, the impurity <span>\(\ce{P4O10}\)</span> is removed by reacting it with calcium oxide. The only product is calcium phosphate, <span>\(\ce{Ca3(PO4)2}\)</span>. How many moles of <span>\(\ce{P4O10}\)</span> react with three moles of calcium oxide?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>0.5</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>1.5</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>3</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>6</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>A.</strong> <span>\(\ce{P4O10 + 6CaO -> 2Ca3(PO4)2}\)</span>, so three moles of CaO react with 0.5 mol of <span>P<sub>4</sub>O<sub>10</sub></span>.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #periodicity-choice-easy-q8 data-answer="B"}
### Question 8 · Acidic chlorides · 2.1 Choice Easy Q8

Which two chlorides give approximately neutral solutions when added to water?

1. <span>\(\ce{MgCl2}\)</span>  2. <span>\(\ce{NaCl}\)</span>  3. <span>\(\ce{SiCl4}\)</span>

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>1 and 3</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>1 and 2</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>2 and 3</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>1, 2 and 3</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>B.</strong> The ionic chlorides <span>MgCl<sub>2</sub></span> and <span>NaCl</span> do not hydrolyse significantly. <span>SiCl<sub>4</sub></span> hydrolyses to give HCl.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #periodicity-choice-easy-q9 data-answer="C"}
### Question 9 · Isoelectronic ions · 2.1 Choice Easy Q9

Which is the order of increasing radius for <span>\(\ce{O^{2-}}\)</span>, Ne and <span>\(\ce{Mg^{2+}}\)</span>?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>\(\ce{O^{2-} < Ne < Mg^{2+}}\)</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>\(\ce{Ne < Mg^{2+} < O^{2-}}\)</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>\(\ce{Mg^{2+} < Ne < O^{2-}}\)</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>\(\ce{Mg^{2+} < O^{2-} < Ne}\)</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>C.</strong> These species each have ten electrons. More protons attract the same electron cloud more strongly, so <span>Mg<sup>2+</sup></span> is smallest and <span>O<sup>2−</sup></span> is largest.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #periodicity-choice-easy-q10 data-answer="A"}
### Question 10 · Electronegativity and first ionisation energy · 2.1 Choice Easy Q10

Which graph correctly shows the relative electronegativities and first ionisation energies of Na, Mg, Al and Si?

<div class="question-figure-grid"><img src="../assets/questions/original-source/2-1-choice-easy-q10-option-a.png" alt="Option A graph"><img src="../assets/questions/original-source/2-1-choice-easy-q10-option-b.png" alt="Option B graph"><img src="../assets/questions/original-source/2-1-choice-easy-q10-option-c.png" alt="Option C graph"><img src="../assets/questions/original-source/2-1-choice-easy-q10-option-d.png" alt="Option D graph"></div>
<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>Graph A</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>Graph B</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>Graph C</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>Graph D</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>A.</strong> Electronegativity increases steadily from Na to Si, while first ionisation energy has the Mg–Al dip because Al loses a 3p electron.</p></details>
:::

### 9 The Periodic Table: chemical periodicity — Multiple Choice: Medium

::: {.mc-question #periodicity-choice-medium-q1 data-answer="D"}
### Question 11 · Hydrolysis of Period 3 chlorides · 2.1 Choice Medium Q1

Which Period 3 chloride does not produce hydrogen chloride fumes when added to water?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>\(\ce{AlCl3}\)</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>\(\ce{SiCl4}\)</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>\(\ce{PCl5}\)</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>\(\ce{MgCl2}\)</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>D.</strong> Magnesium chloride is an ionic chloride and dissolves without significant hydrolysis. The other three chlorides hydrolyse and produce HCl.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #periodicity-choice-medium-q2 data-answer="C"}
### Question 12 · Melting points of chlorides · 2.1 Choice Medium Q2

Which order gives decreasing melting point for HCl, <span>\(\ce{MgCl2}\)</span>, <span>\(\ce{CCl4}\)</span> and <span>\(\ce{S2Cl2}\)</span>?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>\(\ce{HCl > CCl4 > S2Cl2 > MgCl2}\)</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>\(\ce{MgCl2 > S2Cl2 > CCl4 > HCl}\)</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>\(\ce{MgCl2 > CCl4 > S2Cl2 > HCl}\)</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>\(\ce{CCl4 > MgCl2 > HCl > S2Cl2}\)</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>C.</strong> The ionic lattice in <span>MgCl<sub>2</sub></span> gives the highest melting point. Among simple molecular substances, larger molecules generally have stronger London forces.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #periodicity-choice-medium-q3 data-answer="A"}
### Question 13 · Consecutive Period 3 elements · 2.1 Choice Medium Q3

X, Y and Z are consecutive Period 3 elements. Y has the highest first ionisation energy and the lowest melting point of the three. Which set is possible?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>X = Si, Y = P, Z = S</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>X = Na, Y = Mg, Z = Al</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>X = P, Y = S, Z = Cl</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>X = Mg, Y = Al, Z = Si</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>A.</strong> Phosphorus has a local maximum in first ionisation energy and is a simple molecular solid with a low melting point compared with silicon.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #periodicity-choice-medium-q4 data-answer="C"}
### Question 14 · Period 4 oxides · 2.1 Choice Medium Q4

Which pair of Period 4 elements forms oxides that give acidic solutions in water?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>Ga and Ge</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>Ge and As</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>As and Se</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>Ga and Se</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>C.</strong> The oxides become more covalent and acidic across the period. Arsenic and selenium form acidic oxides; gallium oxide is amphoteric and germanium oxide is less strongly acidic.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #periodicity-choice-medium-q5 data-answer="C"}
### Question 15 · Melting point and electronegativity · 2.1 Choice Medium Q5

Which graph correctly shows the relationship between melting point and electronegativity for Mg, Al, Si and P?

<div class="question-figure-grid"><img src="../assets/questions/original-source/2-1-choice-medium-q5-option-a.png" alt="Option A graph"><img src="../assets/questions/original-source/2-1-choice-medium-q5-option-b.png" alt="Option B graph"><img src="../assets/questions/original-source/2-1-choice-medium-q5-option-c.png" alt="Option C graph"><img src="../assets/questions/original-source/2-1-choice-medium-q5-option-d.png" alt="Option D graph"></div>
<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>Graph A</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>Graph B</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>Graph C</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>Graph D</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>C.</strong> Silicon has a giant covalent structure and the highest melting point; phosphorus is simple molecular and has the lowest. Electronegativity increases from Mg to P.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #periodicity-choice-medium-q6 data-answer="A"}
### Question 16 · Structure and properties · 2.1 Choice Medium Q6

Which statement about silicon dioxide, sodium chloride and aluminium is correct?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>Silicon dioxide has a giant covalent structure, sodium chloride has a giant ionic structure, and aluminium conducts electricity as a solid.</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>All three substances contain simple covalent molecules.</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>Sodium chloride conducts electricity as a solid because its ions are mobile.</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>Silicon dioxide has a low melting point because it contains weak intermolecular forces.</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>A.</strong> The structures are giant covalent, giant ionic and metallic respectively. Delocalised electrons allow aluminium to conduct as a solid.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #periodicity-choice-medium-q7 data-answer="A"}
### Question 17 · 3p electrons and acidic oxides · 2.1 Choice Medium Q7

Which combination is correct for sulfur and phosphorus?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>Sulfur has an oxide that forms a strong acid in water; phosphorus has no paired 3p electrons and also forms an acidic oxide.</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>Sulfur has no paired 3p electrons; phosphorus forms only a basic oxide.</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>Neither element forms an acidic oxide.</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>Only sulfur has no paired 3p electrons.</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>A.</strong> Sulfur has a paired 3p electron, whereas phosphorus has a 3p<sup>3</sup> configuration. Both can form acidic oxides.</p></details>
:::

### 9 The Periodic Table: chemical periodicity — Multiple Choice: Hard

::: {.mc-question #periodicity-choice-hard-q1 data-answer="A"}
### Question 18 · Aluminium chloride observations · 2.1 Choice Hard Q1

Which set of observations is inconsistent with aluminium chloride?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>It gives a solution of pH 12 and has a melting point close to that of sodium chloride.</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>It is a white crystalline solid and its solution is acidic.</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>It has a lower melting point than expected for a purely ionic lattice.</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>It hydrolyses in water and produces hydrogen ions.</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>A.</strong> Aluminium chloride hydrolyses to give an acidic solution, not pH 12. Its covalent character also gives it a much lower melting point than sodium chloride.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #periodicity-choice-hard-q2 data-answer="C"}
### Question 19 · Amphoteric aluminium oxide · 2.1 Choice Hard Q2

The original scheme shows the reactions of an unknown element X.

![Original reaction sequence for X](../assets/questions/original-source/2-1-choice-hard-q2-figure.png){.question-figure fig-alt="Reaction sequence showing combustion, acid reaction and amphoteric hydroxide"}

Which element could be X?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>Mg</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>Si</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>Al</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>P</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>C.</strong> Aluminium burns to form amphoteric <span>Al<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub></span>. It reacts with acid, then gives <span>Al(OH)<sub>3</sub></span> which dissolves in excess sodium hydroxide.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #periodicity-choice-hard-q3 data-answer="D"}
### Question 20 · Successive trends in Group 2 · 2.1 Choice Hard Q3

Four elements are Davy's elements: Mg, B, Na and Ca. Which element has the third-lowest first ionisation energy in its period and the third-smallest atomic radius in its group?

<div class="mc-options"><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>Mg</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>B</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>Na</span></button><button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>Ca</span></button></div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>D.</strong> Group 2 elements have the third-lowest first ionisation energy in their periods because the Group 3 p electron is easier to remove. The third-smallest Group 2 radius is the Period 4 member, calcium.</p></details>
:::
